articles.title: 完型 · 肥胖、BMI与健康偏见
articles.context: 讨论体重、BMI与健康之间并非简单线性关系，并分析社会对肥胖的污名与反肥胖政策。语气应理性、医学科普化，转折处清楚但不过度表演。
rows: Thinner isn't always better.
更瘦并不总是更好。
advance
A number of studies have concluded that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight.
多项研究已经得出结论：事实上，与超重者相比，体重正常的人患某些疾病的风险反而更高。
explain
And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually protective.
而且在某些健康状况下，超重实际上具有保护作用。
advance
For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women.
例如，体重较重的女性比瘦女性更不容易出现钙缺乏。
example
Likewise among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an indicator of good health.
同样，在老年人中，略微超重往往是健康状况良好的一个指标。
compare
Of even greater concern is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define.
更值得关注的是，事实证明，肥胖其实很难界定。
emphasize
It is often defined in terms of body mass index, or BMI.
人们常常依据身体质量指数，也就是 BMI，来界定肥胖。
explain
BMI equals body mass divided by the square of height.
BMI 等于体重除以身高的平方。
explain
An adult with a BMI of 18 to 25 is often considered to be normal weight.
成年人的 BMI 在18至25之间，通常被认为体重正常。
report
Between 25 and 30 is overweight.
BMI 在25至30之间属于超重。
sequence
And over 30 is considered obese.
而超过30则被认为属于肥胖。
report
Obesity, in turn, can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese.
肥胖又可进一步分为中度肥胖、重度肥胖和极重度肥胖。
sequence
While such numerical standards seem straightforward, they are not.
尽管这类数字化标准看起来直截了当，实际却并非如此。
contrast
Obesity is probably less a matter of weight than body fat.
与其说肥胖取决于体重，不如说它更多取决于体脂。
qualify
Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, while others with a low BMI may be in poor shape.
有些 BMI 很高的人其实身体非常健壮，而另一些 BMI 很低的人身体状况却可能很差。
contrast
For example, many collegiate and professional football players qualify as obese, though their percentage body fat is low.
例如，许多大学和职业橄榄球运动员按标准会被归为肥胖，尽管他们的体脂率很低。
example
Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a normal BMI.
反过来，骨架较小的人可能体脂很高，但 BMI 仍处于正常范围。
contrast
Today we have a tendency to label obesity as a disgrace.
如今，我们有一种把肥胖贴上“可耻”标签的倾向。
advance
The overweight are sometimes pictured in the media with their faces covered.
媒体有时会刊登超重者的照片，并把他们的脸遮住。
example
Stereotypes associated with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success.
与肥胖相关的刻板印象包括懒惰、缺乏意志力，以及较低的成功前景。
explain
Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese.
研究表明，教师、雇主和医疗专业人员都可能对肥胖者怀有偏见。
report
Even very young children tend to look down on the overweight, and teasing about body build has long been a problem in schools.
甚至年幼的孩子也往往看不起超重者，而拿体形开玩笑长期以来一直是学校里的一个问题。
emphasize
Negative attitudes toward obesity, grounded in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity policies.
以健康担忧为基础的肥胖负面态度，已经推动了多项反肥胖政策。
conclude
My own hospital system has banned sugary drinks from its facilities.
我所在的医院系统已经禁止在其设施内销售含糖饮料。
example
Many employers have instituted weight loss and fitness initiatives.
许多雇主也已推出减重和健身举措。
example
Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign against childhood obesity, even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat.
米歇尔·奥巴马还发起了一场高度引人注目的反儿童肥胖运动，甚至声称儿童肥胖代表着美国最大的国家安全威胁。
emphasize

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 怎样花钱才能获得更持久的幸福
articles.context: 借一位彩票大奖得主切入《Happy Money》的研究结论：体验、关系、给予与稀缺性往往比物质消费更能带来持久满足。语气理性、轻松，适度保留作者的幽默。
rows: What would you do with $590m?
如果你有5.9亿美元，你会怎么花？
ask
This is now a question for Gloria MacKenzie, an 84-year-old widow who recently emerged from her small, tin-roofed house in Florida to collect the biggest undivided lottery jackpot in history.
如今，这正是84岁的寡妇格洛丽亚·麦肯齐要面对的问题：她最近从佛罗里达那座带锡皮屋顶的小房子里走出来，领取了史上金额最大的单人彩票头奖。
story
If she hopes her new-found fortune will yield lasting feelings of fulfilment, she could do worse than read Happy Money by Elizabeth Dunn and Michael Norton.
如果她希望这笔新得的财富能带来持久的满足感，那么读一读伊丽莎白·邓恩和迈克尔·诺顿合著的《幸福金钱》，不失为一个好选择。
advance
These two academics use an array of behavioral research to show that the most rewarding ways to spend money can be counterintuitive.
这两位学者借助一系列行为研究表明，最能带来回报的花钱方式有时是反直觉的。
explain
Fantasies of great wealth often involve visions of fancy cars and extravagant homes.
人们幻想巨额财富时，常会想到豪车和奢华的住宅。
example
Yet satisfaction with these material purchases wears off fairly quickly.
然而，这些物质消费带来的满足很快就会消退。
contrast
What was once exciting and new becomes old-hat; regret creeps in.
曾经令人兴奋的新鲜事物会变得司空见惯，懊悔也随之悄然滋生。
conclude
It is far better to spend money on experiences, say Ms Dunn and Mr Norton, like interesting trips, unique meals or even going to the cinema.
邓恩和诺顿认为，把钱花在体验上要好得多，比如有趣的旅行、独特的一餐，甚至只是去看一场电影。
contrast
These purchases often become more valuable with time - as stories or memories - particularly if they involve feeling more connected to others.
这类消费往往会随着时间推移，以故事或记忆的形式变得更有价值，尤其是在它们能让人感到与他人联系更紧密时。
explain
This slim volume is packed with tips to help wage slaves as well as lottery winners get the most "happiness bang for your buck."
这本薄薄的书里装满了实用建议，既帮助工薪族，也帮助彩票赢家，让每一块钱尽可能换来更多幸福。
advance

It seems most people would be better off if they could shorten their commutes to work, spend more time with friends and family and less of it watching television (something the average American spends a whopping two months a year doing, and is hardly jollier for it).
看来，如果人们能缩短通勤时间，多陪朋友和家人，少看一些电视，生活会更好；普通美国人一年竟有足足两个月花在看电视上，却几乎没有因此更快乐。
explain
Buying gifts or giving to charity is often more pleasurable than purchasing things for oneself, and luxuries are most enjoyable when they are consumed sparingly.
买礼物送人或捐给慈善机构，往往比给自己买东西更令人愉快；而奢侈品只有在有节制地享用时最让人愉悦。
compare
This is apparently the reason McDonald's restricts the availability of its popular McRib - a marketing trick that has turned the pork sandwich into an object of obsession.
这显然就是麦当劳限制热门产品 McRib 供应的原因：这种营销手法把一个猪肉三明治变成了令人痴迷的对象。
example
Readers of Happy Money are clearly a privileged lot, anxious about fulfilment, not hunger.
显然，《幸福金钱》的读者属于较为优裕的一群，他们焦虑的是满足感，而不是饥饿。
qualify
Money may not quite buy happiness, but people in wealthier countries are generally happier than those in poor ones.
金钱也许不能直接买到幸福，但富裕国家的人总体上确实比贫穷国家的人更快乐。
contrast
Yet the link between feeling good and spending money on others can be seen among rich and poor people around the world, and scarcity enhances the pleasure of most things for most people.
不过，在世界各地，无论贫富，人们都能看到为他人花钱与感觉良好之间的联系，而且稀缺性会增强大多数人从大多数事物中获得的快乐。
contrast
Not everyone will agree with the authors' policy ideas, which range from mandating more holiday time to reducing tax incentives for American homebuyers.
并非所有人都会赞同作者的政策主张，从强制增加休假时间，到削减美国购房者的税收激励，这些主张跨度很大。
qualify
But most people will come away from this book believing it was money well spent.
但大多数人读完这本书后，都会觉得这笔钱花得值。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 我们为何往往觉得自己比实际更好看
articles.context: 介绍“高于平均水平效应”和自我美化研究，解释人们如何在记忆、照片与社交媒体中维持更积极的自我形象。语气是清晰的心理学科普。
rows: An article in Scientific American has pointed out that empirical research says that, actually, you think you're more beautiful than you are.
《科学美国人》的一篇文章指出，实证研究表明：事实上，你往往觉得自己比实际更漂亮。
advance
We have a deep-seated need to feel good about ourselves and we naturally employ a number of self-enhancing strategies to achieve this.
我们内心深处需要对自己感觉良好，因此会自然而然地采用多种自我美化策略来达到这一目的。
explain

Social psychologists have amassed oceans of research into what they call the "above average effect", or "illusory superiority", and shown that, for example, 70% of us rate ourselves as above average in leadership, 93% in driving and 85% at getting on well with others - all obviously statistical impossibilities.
社会心理学家已经积累了大量有关所谓“高于平均水平效应”或“虚幻优越感”的研究，并发现：例如，70%的人认为自己的领导力高于平均水平，93%的人认为自己的驾驶水平高于平均水平，85%的人认为自己与人相处的能力高于平均水平——从统计上看，这些显然都不可能同时成立。
statistic
We rose-tint our memories and put ourselves into self-affirming situations.
我们会给自己的记忆染上一层玫瑰色，也会把自己置于能够肯定自我的情境中。
explain
We become defensive when criticised, and apply negative stereotypes to others to boost our own esteem.
受到批评时，我们会转入防御状态，还会把负面的刻板印象套在别人身上，以抬高自己的自尊。
explain
We stalk around thinking we're hot stuff.
我们昂首走来走去，觉得自己相当了不起。
irony
Psychologist and behavioural scientist Nicholas Epley oversaw a key study into self-enhancement and attractiveness.
心理学家兼行为科学家尼古拉斯·埃普利主持了一项关于自我美化与吸引力的重要研究。
advance

Rather than have people simply rate their beauty compared with others, he asked them to identify an original photograph of themselves from a lineup including versions that had been altered to appear more and less attractive.
他没有让受试者简单评价自己相较他人的外貌，而是让他们从一组照片中找出自己的原始照片；这组照片里还混入了经过处理、显得更好看或更不好看的版本。
contrast
Visual recognition, reads the study, is "an automatic psychological process, occurring rapidly and intuitively with little or no apparent conscious deliberation".
研究写道，视觉识别是“一种自动的心理过程，会迅速而直觉地发生，几乎不需要或完全不需要明显的有意识深思”。
explain_quote
If the subjects quickly chose a falsely flattering image - which most did - they genuinely believed it was really how they looked.
如果受试者很快选中了那张经过美化、却并不真实的照片——而大多数人确实如此——那说明他们真心相信自己就是那个样子。
conclude
Epley found no significant gender difference in responses.
埃普利发现，男女受试者的反应并没有显著差异。
report

Nor was there any evidence that those who self-enhanced the most (that is, the participants who thought the most positively doctored pictures were real) were doing so to make up for profound insecurities.
也没有证据表明，那些自我美化程度最高的人——也就是把美化得最明显的照片当成真实照片的人——这样做是为了弥补深层的不安全感。
contrast
In fact, those who thought that the images higher up the attractiveness scale were real directly corresponded with those who showed other markers for having higher self-esteem.
事实上，越是把吸引力评分更高的照片当作真实照片的人，越会同时表现出其他高自尊的指标。
emphasize
"I don't think the findings that we have are any evidence of personal delusion," says Epley.
埃普利说：“我不认为我们的研究结果能证明个人存在妄想。”
dialogue
"It's a reflection simply of people generally thinking well of themselves."
“它只不过反映了人们通常对自己评价不错。”
explain_quote
If you are depressed, you won't be self-enhancing.
如果你处于抑郁状态，就不会进行这种自我美化。
qualify
Knowing the results of Epley's study, it makes sense that many people hate photographs of themselves viscerally - on one level, they don't even recognise the person in the picture as themselves.
了解埃普利的研究结果后，就不难理解为什么很多人会本能地讨厌自己的照片：在某种层面上，他们甚至认不出照片里的人就是自己。
conclude
Facebook, therefore, is a self-enhancer's paradise, where people can share only the most flattering photos, the cream of their wit, style, beauty, intellect and lifestyles.
因此，Facebook 堪称自我美化者的天堂：人们可以只展示最上镜的照片，以及自己机智、品位、美貌、才智和生活方式中最光鲜的一面。
conclude
It's not that people's profiles are dishonest, says Catalina Toma of Wisconsin-Madison University, "but they portray an idealised version of themselves."
威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的卡塔利娜·托马说，人们的个人主页并非不诚实，“只是呈现了一个理想化的自己”。
qualify_quote

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 与机器竞赛，还是与机器协作
articles.context: 讨论自动化对就业的冲击，并借 John Hagel 的观点把问题从“机器取代人”转向工作设计与制度创新。语气应有科技评论的推进感。
rows: The concept of man versus machine is at least as old as the industrial revolution, but this phenomenon tends to be most acutely felt during economic downturns and fragile recoveries.
“人与机器对抗”这一观念至少和工业革命一样古老，但在经济衰退和脆弱复苏时期，人们对这种现象的感受往往最为强烈。
advance
And yet, it would be a mistake to think we are right now simply experiencing the painful side of a boom and bust cycle.
然而，如果认为我们现在只是正在经历繁荣—萧条周期痛苦的一面，那就错了。
contrast
Certain jobs have gone away for good, outmoded by machines.
有些工作已经永久消失，被机器淘汰了。
emphasize
Since technology has such an insatiable appetite for eating up human jobs, this phenomenon will continue to restructure our economy in ways we cannot immediately foresee.
由于技术对吞噬人类工作岗位有着近乎贪得无厌的胃口，这一现象还会继续以我们暂时无法预见的方式重塑经济。
warning
When there is rapid improvement in the price and performance of technology, jobs that were once thought to be immune from automation suddenly become threatened.
当技术的价格与性能迅速改善时，那些曾被认为不会受到自动化影响的工作会突然面临威胁。
explain
This argument has attracted a lot of attention, via the success of the book Race Against the Machine, by Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee, who both hail from MIT's Center for Digital Business.
这一论点随着埃里克·布林约尔松和安德鲁·麦卡菲所著《与机器赛跑》的走红而受到广泛关注；两位作者都来自麻省理工学院数字商业中心。
report
This is a powerful argument, and a scary one.
这个论点很有力量，也令人不安。
emphasize
And yet, John Hagel, author of The Power of Pull and other books, says Brynjolfsson and McAfee miss the reason why these jobs are so vulnerable to technology in the first place.
不过，《拉力的力量》等书的作者约翰·哈格尔认为，布林约尔松和麦卡菲忽略了这些工作为何从一开始就如此容易受到技术冲击。
contrast
Hagel says we have designed jobs in the U.S. that tend to be "tightly scripted" and "highly standardized" ones that leave no room for "individual initiative or creativity".
哈格尔说，美国设计出的许多工作往往“程序严密”“高度标准化”，不给“个人主动性或创造力”留下空间。
explain_quote
In short, these are the types of jobs that machines can perform much better at than human beings.
简而言之，这类工作恰恰是机器比人做得好得多的工作。
conclude
That is how we have put a giant target sign on the backs of American workers, Hagel says.
哈格尔说，我们正是这样在美国劳动者背后画上了一个巨大的靶心。
evaluation_quote
It's time to reinvent the formula for how work is conducted, since we are still relying on a very 20th century notion of work, Hagel says.
哈格尔认为，是时候重新设计工作的运作方式了，因为我们仍然依赖一种非常20世纪的工作观。
action_turn
In our rapidly changing economy, we more than ever need people in the workplace who can take initiative and exercise their imagination "to respond to unexpected events".
在快速变化的经济中，我们比以往任何时候都更需要能在职场中发挥主动性、运用想象力“应对意外事件”的人。
emphasize
That is not something machines are good at.
而这并不是机器擅长的事情。
contrast
They are designed to perform very predictable activities.
机器被设计出来，是为了执行高度可预测的活动。
explain
As Hagel notes, Brynjolfsson and McAfee indeed touched on this point in their book.
正如哈格尔所指出的，布林约尔松和麦卡菲的确在书中谈到了这一点。
qualify
We need to reframe race against the machine as race with the machine.
我们需要把“与机器赛跑”重新理解为“和机器一起赛跑”。
emphasize
In other words, we need to look at the ways in which machines can augment human labor rather than replace it.
换言之，我们应当关注机器怎样增强人类劳动，而不是怎样取代人类劳动。
explain
So then the problem is not really about technology, but rather, "how do we innovate our institutions and our work practices?"
因此，真正的问题并不在技术本身，而在于“我们如何创新我们的制度和工作实践？”
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 英国住房为何应被视为基础设施问题
articles.context: 从英国政策与财政角度论证住房对经济增长的重要性，讨论可负担住房、地方借贷上限、租赁环境与公共拨款。采用成熟克制的英式政策评论语气。
rows: When the government talks about infrastructure contributing to the economy the focus is usually on roads, railways, broadband and energy.
政府谈到基础设施如何促进经济时，通常关注的是公路、铁路、宽带和能源。
advance
Housing is seldom mentioned.
住房却很少被提及。
contrast
Why is that?
为什么会这样？
ask
To some extent the housing sector must shoulder the blame.
在一定程度上，住房行业本身也必须承担责任。
qualify
We have not been good at communicating the real value that housing can contribute to economic growth.
我们并不善于向外界说明住房能够为经济增长贡献的真实价值。
explain
Then there is the scale of the typical housing project.
其次，还有一般住房项目的规模问题。
sequence
It is hard to shove for attention among multibillion-pound infrastructure projects, so it is inevitable that the attention is focused elsewhere.
与动辄数十亿英镑的基础设施项目争夺关注并不容易，因此注意力转向别处也就不可避免。
explain
But perhaps the most significant reason is that the issue has always been so politically charged.
但最重要的原因或许在于，住房问题一直具有如此强烈的政治色彩。
emphasize
Nevertheless, the affordable housing situation is desperate.
尽管如此，可负担住房的形势已经十分严峻。
contrast
Waiting lists increase all the time and we are simply not building enough new homes.
等候名单不断变长，而我们建造的新住房就是不够。
explain
The comprehensive spending review offers an opportunity for the government to help rectify this.
全面支出审查给政府提供了帮助纠正这一局面的机会。
advance
It needs to put historical prejudices to one side and take some steps to address our urgent housing need.
政府需要把历史成见放到一边，采取措施应对迫切的住房需求。
action_turn
There are some indications that it is preparing to do just that.
有一些迹象表明，政府正准备这样做。
report

The communities minister, Don Foster, has hinted that George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, may introduce more flexibility to the current cap on the amount that local authorities can borrow against their housing stock debt.
社区事务大臣唐·福斯特暗示，财政大臣乔治·奥斯本可能会提高现有借款上限的灵活性；这一上限目前限制着地方政府以其住房存量债务为基础所能借入的金额。
report
Evidence shows that 60,000 extra new homes could be built over the next five years if the cap were lifted, increasing GDP by 0.6%.
证据显示，如果取消这一上限，未来五年可以额外建造6万套新住房，并使 GDP 增长0.6%。
statistic

Ministers should also look at creating greater certainty in the rental environment, which would have a significant impact on the ability of registered providers to fund new developments from revenues.
大臣们还应考虑让租赁环境具有更大的确定性，因为这会显著影响注册住房提供者依靠收入为新开发项目融资的能力。
action_turn
But it is not just down to the government.
但责任并不只在政府。
contrast

While these measures would be welcome in the short term, we must face up to the fact that the existing £4.5bn programme of grants to fund new affordable housing, set to expire in 2015, is unlikely to be extended beyond then.
虽然这些措施在短期内会受到欢迎，但我们必须面对这样一个事实：现有的45亿英镑可负担住房拨款计划将在2015年到期，此后不太可能继续延长。
contrast
The Labour party has recently announced that it will retain a large part of the coalition's spending plans if it returns to power.
工党最近宣布，如果重新执政，它将保留联合政府支出计划中的很大一部分。
report
The housing sector needs to accept that we are very unlikely to ever return to the era of large-scale public grants.
住房行业需要接受一个现实：我们几乎不可能再回到大规模公共拨款的时代。
warning
We need to adjust to this changing climate.
我们需要适应这种正在变化的环境。
action_turn
While the government's commitment to long-term funding may have changed, the very pressing need for more affordable housing is real and is not going away.
尽管政府对长期资金支持的承诺可能已经改变，但增加可负担住房的迫切需求是真实存在的，而且不会自行消失。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 英国土地艺术的作品与观念
articles.context: 介绍20世纪六七十年代英国土地艺术及多件代表作品，比较其与美国土地艺术的差异，并说明其浪漫主义、观念艺术和画廊属性。采用清晰优雅的英式文化解说语气。
rows: Emerging in the late Sixties and reaching a peak in the Seventies, Land Art was one of a range of new forms, including Body Art, Performance Art, Action Art and Installation Art, which pushed art beyond the traditional confines of the studio and gallery.
土地艺术兴起于20世纪60年代末，在70年代达到高峰；它与身体艺术、表演艺术、行动艺术和装置艺术等一系列新形式一道，把艺术推向工作室和画廊的传统界限之外。
advance
Rather than portraying landscape, land artists used the physical substance of the land itself as their medium.
土地艺术家并不描绘风景，而是直接把土地的物质实体当作创作媒介。
contrast
The British land art, typified by Richard Long's piece, was not only more domestically scaled, but a lot quirkier than its American counterpart.
以理查德·朗的作品为代表，英国土地艺术不仅规模更为本土化，也比美国的对应形式古怪得多。
compare
Indeed, while you might assume that an exhibition of Land Art would consist only of records of works rather than the works themselves, Long's photograph of his work is the work.
的确，你也许会以为土地艺术展览只能陈列作品的记录，而非作品本身；但朗拍摄自己作品的照片，本身就是作品。
contrast
Since his "action" is in the past, the photograph is its sole embodiment.
由于他的“行动”已经发生在过去，这张照片便成了那次行动唯一的实体化呈现。
conclude
That might seem rather an obscure point, but it sets the tone for an exhibition that contains a lot of black-and-white photographs and relatively few natural objects.
这一点也许显得颇为晦涩，却为整场展览定下了基调：大量黑白照片与相对少量的自然物件。
qualify
Long is Britain's best-known Land Artist and his Stone Circle, a perfect ring of purplish rocks from Portishead beach laid out on the gallery floor, represents the elegant, rarefied side of the form.
朗是英国最著名的土地艺术家；他的《石圈》由波蒂斯黑德海滩的紫色岩石在画廊地面围成一个完美圆环，代表了这种艺术优雅而精炼的一面。
example
The Boyle Family, on the other hand, stand for its dirty, urban aspect.
而博伊尔家族则代表了它肮脏、都市化的一面。
contrast
Comprising artists Mark Boyle and Joan Hills and their children, they recreated random sections of the British landscape on gallery walls.
这个家庭艺术团体由马克·博伊尔、琼·希尔斯和他们的孩子组成，他们把英国景观中随机截取的区域重新呈现在画廊墙面上。
explain

Their Olaf Street Study, a square of brick-strewn waste ground, is one of the few works here to embrace the commonplaceness that characterises most of our experience of the landscape most of the time.
他们的《奥拉夫街研究》呈现一块散落着砖头的方形荒地，是展览中少数拥抱日常平凡性的作品之一，而这种平凡恰恰构成了我们大多数时候对景观的实际体验。
example

Parks feature, particularly in the earlier works, such as John Hilliard's very funny Across the Park, in which a long-haired stroller is variously smiled at by a pretty girl and unwittingly assaulted in a sequence of images that turn out to be different parts of the same photograph.
公园在作品中屡屡出现，尤其是在早期作品里；例如约翰·希利亚德颇为诙谐的《穿过公园》，一名长发散步者在一连串图像中时而得到漂亮女孩的微笑，时而在不知情中遭到袭击，而这些图像最终被发现都来自同一张照片的不同部分。
story
Generally however British land artists preferred to get away from towns, gravitating towards landscapes that are traditionally considered beautiful such as the Lake District or the Wiltshire Downs.
不过总体而言，英国土地艺术家更愿意远离城镇，趋向湖区或威尔特郡丘陵这类传统上被认为优美的景观。
contrast
While it probably wasn't apparent at the time, much of this work is permeated by a spirit of romantic escapism that the likes of Wordsworth would have readily understood.
尽管当时人们也许没有明显意识到，但这些作品中有很大一部分都渗透着浪漫主义逃避现实的精神，像华兹华斯这样的人会很容易理解它。
qualify

Derek Jarman's yellow-tinted film Towards Avebury, a collection of long, mostly still shots of the Wiltshire landscape, evokes a tradition of English landscape painting stretching from Samuel Palmer to Paul Nash.
德里克·贾曼的黄调电影《走向埃夫伯里》由一组威尔特郡景观的长镜头构成，大多近乎静止，它唤起了从塞缪尔·帕尔默延续到保罗·纳什的英国风景画传统。
example
In the case of Hamish Fulton, you can't help feeling that the Scottish artist has simply found a way of making his love of walking pay.
说到哈米什·富尔顿，你很难不觉得，这位苏格兰艺术家不过是找到了一种让自己对徒步的热爱产生收益的方式。
irony
A typical work, such as Seven Days, consists of a single beautiful black-and-white photograph taken on an epic walk, with the mileage and number of days taken listed beneath.
他的典型作品如《七天》，只包含一张在一次漫长徒步途中拍摄的漂亮黑白照片，照片下方列出行走里程和所用天数。
example

British Land Art as shown in this well selected, but relatively modestly scaled exhibition wasn't about imposing on the landscape, more a kind of landscape-orientated light conceptual art created passing through.
这场选品精当但规模相对不大的展览所呈现的英国土地艺术，并不是要把某种意志强加于景观，而更像是一种在穿行过程中生成、以景观为导向的轻观念艺术。
evaluation_quote
It had its origins in the great outdoors, but the results were as gallery-bound as the paintings of Turner and Constable.
它起源于广阔的户外，但最终成果却和透纳、康斯特布尔的绘画一样，被牢牢地带回了画廊。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 现实主义的健康乐观
articles.context: 解释积极心理学所说的“健康乐观”：接触现实、允许自己不完美、复盘并拉开人生视角。语气温和、清楚、有安定感。
rows: Most people would define optimism as being endlessly happy, with a glass that's perpetually half full.
大多数人会把乐观定义为永远快乐，仿佛杯子永远都是半满的。
advance
But that's exactly the kind of false cheerfulness that positive psychologists wouldn't recommend.
但这恰恰是积极心理学家不会提倡的那种虚假乐观。
contrast
"Healthy optimism means being in touch with reality," says Tal Ben-Shahar, a Harvard professor.
哈佛大学教授塔尔·本-沙哈尔说：“健康的乐观意味着与现实保持接触。”
dialogue
According to Ben-Shahar, realistic optimists are those who make the best of things that happen, but not those who believe everything happens for the best.
本-沙哈尔认为，现实主义的乐观者，是那些能从已经发生的事情中尽可能获得最好结果的人，而不是相信凡事都会自动朝最好方向发展的人。
contrast
Ben-Shahar uses three optimistic exercises.
本-沙哈尔会采用三种乐观练习。
sequence
When he feels down - say, after giving a bad lecture - he grants himself permission to be human.
当他情绪低落时——比如一堂课讲得不好之后——他会允许自己只是一个普通人。
story
He reminds himself that not every lecture can be a Nobel winner; some will be less effective than others.
他会提醒自己，不是每一堂课都能达到“诺贝尔奖级别”；有些课的效果就是会比另一些差。
explain
Next is reconstruction.
接下来是复盘重构。
sequence
He analyzes the weak lecture, learning lessons for the future about what works and what doesn't.
他分析那堂表现不佳的课，从中总结哪些方法有效、哪些无效，为今后汲取经验。
explain
Finally, there is perspective, which involves acknowledging that in the grand scheme of life, one lecture really doesn't matter.
最后是拉开视角：承认从整个人生的大格局来看，一堂课其实真的没有那么重要。
conclude
